findings.title: canManage() grants global group manage to holders of VIEW-only all-groups permission
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so it returns true for an admin whose all-groups permission only grants the `view` scope. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `requireManage()`, so a view-only admin can create top-level groups and move existing groups to top level. The check should require only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE`. The interface javadoc for `canManage()` repeats the same wrong "VIEW or MANAGE" statement and should be corrected too.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource IDs, not group IDs, and resolves the wrong resource
findings.body:
In V2, per-group resources are created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` with the group ID as the resource name and no type set. Only the 'Groups' all-resource has type `Groups`. As a result:
- `findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` does not enumerate the per-group resources.
- `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` passes a resource ID where a group ID (resource name) is expected, so `findByName` misses and evaluation falls back to the all-groups resource.
- `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds an authz resource ID instead of a group ID.

The returned set is used as `UserModel.GROUPS` in user search and in `getUsersCount`. Users counts and DB-level group filtering for admins with group-based view-members permissions will therefore be wrong: wrong counts, and pagination applied before the in-memory `canView` filter.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-groups resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: When no per-group resource exists, `getResourceTypeResource(...)` can return null. This happens if the realm does not have admin permissions enabled, or if the `Groups` resource is missing, for example in a realm whose admin-permissions client was initialized before the Groups type was added to the schema. The null is then passed to `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later dereferenced via `resource.getScopes()`. Existing realms initialized with only the Users/Clients schema would hit this on any group permission check. Return false when `resource` is null.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc references the wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it throws if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false. The implementation actually checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. The `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` javadoc also says it returns a "Stream" while the method returns a `Set`.
